what_this_is: The machine-readable spine of the mid-term single-repository review panel.
Every constant here is cross-checked against scripts/midtermpanel/ by
so this document and the code cannot drift apart without a test failing. A
governance file that merely describes what the code is supposed to do is a
comment with a digest. (This line used to name a function,
`midtermpanel.policy.assert_matches_code`, that has never existed in this
repository — a governance document claiming a mechanism it does not have is
the same defect the state ladder below exists to prevent.)
what_this_is_not: This is NOT the trusted lane. It is not write-separated, it holds a
repository-scoped Actions secret in the repository it reviews, it rests on
no recorded operator prerequisite, and no protected environment gates it.
Nothing produced under this policy may be labelled TRUSTED_*, independent,

ci_operational_state_history_evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_IN_PROGRESS -> STAGED_NO_PROVIDER_SECRET. The panel workflow merged to main as PR #37 (merge 8644935e) and PR #38 (merge 27bfefb5). The hosted no-key vertical `midterm-panel-dry-run` ran green from a clean clone with `permissions: contents: read` and no `secrets.` reference of any kind, and the repository secret named by `secret.name` held a three-space placeholder rather than a usable provider credential throughout. The document was never advanced at the time, which is why this rung is recorded here rather than inferred from the file's history.

STAGED_NO_PROVIDER_SECRET -> STAGED_PROVIDER_KEY_PRESENT_NO_CALLS. A usable provider key was installed by the operator, and the engine release the panel is bound to now exists: tag `midterm-panel-engine-2026-08-10`, built by run 31427275863 from exact default-branch SHA 27bfefb5 with `github.ref_protected` reported as false. `governance/midterm-panel-engine-release.json` names all seven binding fields, and `midterm-engine-release-validation` materialises that exact release asset and validates it in a job that holds no provider credential and can open no socket to a provider host. No provider or generation call has been made.

STAGED_PROVIDER_KEY_PRESENT_NO_CALLS -> PROVIDER_ATTEMPTS_OBSERVED_NOT_ACTIVE. Panel run 31718284187 (midterm-count job 94508561279) reviewed candidate head 14a9b3225e2563d0475b7b662d4b556489dc2342 against tested base 512e81e31b21edafb440937718cd8912c3326c59. It made ONE real provider count attempt and the provider answered 400 invalid_request_error / invalid_json_schema at param=text.format.schema. Durable accounting: provider_attempts=1, count_attempts=1, generation_attempts=0, journal_present=true, accounting_complete=true, accounting_state=ATTEMPTS_KNOWN_NONZERO. No count evidence and no panel evidence were produced; midterm-panel was skipped; the terminal status was midterm-panel-count=error. The previous state's claim that no provider call had been made became false at that moment, and ACTIVE remained false because no review completed. A further 16 operator diagnostic calls were made against the count endpoint only, to isolate the rejected schema keyword; those are diagnostics, not panel votes and not panel evidence.
architecture.state_history_honest_scope: The ordered walk that reached the declared state. `policystate.assert_recorded_history_is_a_legal_walk` re-walks it through the same `assert_transition` a live transition uses, so a history that starts halfway up the ladder, takes a forbidden step, or ends somewhere other than the declared state is a failing test. It cannot verify that each step's evidence exists — the prose above is an operator record, not a proof.
first_provider_backed_run_note: The one field that stands between a merged activation and an automatic
panel that spends. It is TRUE: the operator authorised the first
provider-backed run in this commit, so `engine.load_engine_for_mode` no
longer refuses at the key-present rung.
The refusal it replaces was OBSERVED before it was removed, which is why
this field could be flipped on evidence rather than on belief. Panel run
31527283777, on PR #40 head 9ee6dbc, reached the gate inside the
credential-bearing count job and refused in 114ms with
`category=first_provider_backed_run_not_authorised`, after the identity
document was materialised and before the engine artifact was built. No
provider or generation call was made on that run.
Until this activation the same protection existed by accident:
`assert_provenance_permits` refused a provider-backed run while the
engine release was unbound, and binding the release would have answered
'may we spend?' as a side effect of answering 'which engine?'. The two
questions are now separate, and this one is an operator decision made in
its own reviewed commit rather than a consequence of another change.
The first spending run is authorised for the pull request whose ordinary
CI is re-run after this lands. A string is still refused, not coerced.
It is read only while ci_operational_state is
MIDTERM_SINGLE_REPO_PANEL_STAGED_PROVIDER_KEY_PRESENT_NO_CALLS; once
ACTIVE has been earned the panel runs normally and this gates nothing.

strict_note: `independent_verify.strict_any_refutation` is OPT-IN and OFF by default:
the reference mechanism greens on 'required approver + one corroborator'
even when a third voice refutes. Mid-term policy turns it ON, because the
plan requires that ANY valid refutation blocks. This differs from the
default on purpose and is recorded here so nobody has to infer it.

why: A manually dispatched workflow runs against a SELECTED REF, and every
checkout in the privileged workflow deliberately omits `ref:`. Under
`workflow_run` that omission is the safety property: definition and
checkout both come from the default branch. Under `workflow_dispatch`
it becomes the hazard: the checkout takes the dispatched ref, so a
dispatch against a branch carrying modified `scripts/midtermpanel`
would execute that branch's code in the jobs holding the provider key.
The runtime approval phrase authenticated the CANDIDATE under review.
It never authenticated the ref supplying the reviewer.
manual.controlled_rerun: Re-run ordinary CI on the same head — Actions UI 'Re-run all jobs', or `gh run rerun <CI_RUN_ID>`. The convenience workflow that used to do this was REMOVED: a workflow_dispatch workflow runs a branch-selected copy, so with a persistent repository secret a branch version of it could reference that secret. That is the same selected-ref hazard that removed the dispatch trigger from the privileged panel, reached through a convenience. No repository workflow with `actions: write` is needed.

policy_profiles.selected_by: MIDTERM_REVIEW_CLASS, derived by preflight.review_class_for from the pull-request number through a CLOSED rule. No caller-supplied free-form name, and no per-PR allowlist: the previous design listed pr-23/pr-25/pr-29 and would have refused every future routine pull request.

ordinary_ci_binding.bound_to: the triggering workflow run, by exact id
ordinary_ci_binding.why: A pull-request CI run checks out a generated refs/pull/N/merge commit, so its green is evidence about a merge of the candidate with a SPECIFIC base. The previous check compared the current PR object's base to current main; both track the branch, so when main advanced they moved together and the check passed while ordinary CI had tested a combination that no longer existed.
